A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we found that the semi-mechanistics approach was better than the simpler null models in terms of probabilistic calibration, but the forecasts were still very uncertain, and this uncertainty was not well reflected in the uncertainty estimates.

probabilistic forecasts can be useful for informing public health decision making during epidemics, but that the quality and usefulness of forecasts will depend on the nature of the epidemic, and on the quality of the data and model fits available at the time.

probabilistic forecasts of the Ebola epidemic in Sierra Leone were of sufficient quality to be useful for decision making at short horizons but that the uncertainty in forecasts was too high for longer time horizons, and that the model variants based on semi-mechanistic modelling performed best in terms of calibration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is important to evaluate the calibration of probabilistic forecasts and to assess whether the uncertainty has been quantitatively represented well.
probabilistic forecasts can be evaluated during an epidemic using a range of metrics, and that this approach is particularly useful when comparing different forecasting models.
a range of different model variants may be used to generate forecasts, but that a systematic approach to evaluation is needed to assess which model variant is most useful in practice.
